p3.original: The iPhone is a global product. Apple does not manufacture the iPhone components, nor does it assemble them. The assembly is done by Foxconn Corporation, a Taiwanese company, at its factories in China and India. But, Samsung, the electronics firm and competitor to Apple, actually supplies many of the parts that make up an iPhone. In earlier models, Samsung parts made up as much as 26% of the total costs of production. And in more recent versions, Samsung manufactures the displays and cameras. In some ways, then, Samsung is both the biggest supplier and biggest competitor for Apple. Why do these two firms work together to produce the iPhone? To understand the economic logic behind international trade, you have to accept, as these firms do, that trade is about mutually beneficial exchange. Samsung is one of the world’s largest electronics parts suppliers. Apple lets Samsung focus on making the best parts, which allows Apple to concentrate on its strength—designing elegant products that are easy to use. If each company (and by extension each country) focuses on what it does best, there will be gains for all through trade.
p3.zh: iPhone是全球产品.苹果公司不制造iPhone组件,也不组装.集会由台湾公司福克斯康公司在中国和印度的工厂进行. 但是,三星,电子公司和苹果公司的竞争对手,实际上供应了构成iPhone的许多部件. 在早期的型号中,三星零件占生产总成本的26%.而在更近的版本中,三星制造了显示器和相机.在某些方面,当时三星既是苹果公司最大的供应商,也是最大的竞争对手. 为什么这两家公司合作生产iPhone? 要理解国际贸易背后的经济逻辑,你必须像这些公司那样,接受贸易是互利的交换。 三星是世界上最大的电子零件供应商之一.苹果让三星专注于制作最好的部件,这使得苹果能够集中力量——设计易于使用的优雅产品. 如果每个公司(并进而说,每个国家)都侧重于它最擅长的工作,那么,通过贸易将给所有人带来收益。

p7.zh: 当一个国家在所有货物上享有绝对优势时会发生什么情况?

p9.original: The Benefits of Reducing Barriers to International Trade
p9.zh: 减少国际贸易障碍的益处

p10.original: We live in a global marketplace. The food on your table might include fresh fruit from Chile, cheese from France, and bottled water from Scotland. Your wireless phone might have been made in Taiwan or Korea. The clothes you wear might be designed in Italy and manufactured in China. The toys you give to a child might have come from India. The car you drive might come from Japan, Germany, or Korea. The gasoline in the tank might be refined from crude oil from Saudi Arabia, Mexico, or Nigeria. As a worker, if your job is involved with farming, machinery, airplanes, cars, scientific instruments, or many other technology-related industries, the odds are good that a hearty proportion of the sales of your employer—and hence the money that pays your salary—comes from export sales. We are all linked by international trade, and the volume of that trade has grown dramatically in the last few decades.
p10.zh: 我们生活在一个全球市场中。 你桌上的食物可能包括来自智利的新鲜水果,来自法国的奶酪,以及来自苏格兰的瓶装水. 你的无线手机可能是在台湾或韩国制造的. 你穿的衣服可能在意大利设计,在中国制造. 你给孩子的玩具可能来自印度 你驾驶的汽车可能来自日本,德国或韩国.油箱中的汽油可能来自沙特阿拉伯、墨西哥或尼日利亚的原油。 作为一名工人,如果你的工作涉及农耕、机械、飞机、汽车、科学仪器或其他许多与技术有关的行业,那么,在你的雇主的销售额中——因此支付你工资的钱——有一部分来自出口销售,这种可能性是好的。 我们都与国际贸易联系在一起,在过去几十年中,这种贸易的数量急剧增长。

p11.original: The first wave of globalization started in the nineteenth century and lasted up to the beginning of World War I. Over that time, global exports as a share of global GDP rose from less than 1% of GDP in 1820 to 9% of GDP in 1913. As the Nobel Prize-winning economist Paul Krugman of Princeton University wrote in 1995:
p11.zh: 第一次全球化浪潮始于十九世纪,一直持续到第一次世界大战开始.在此期间,全球出口占全球国内生产总值的比例从1820年不到1%上升到1913年的9%。 正如普林斯顿大学诺贝尔奖得主保罗·克鲁格曼(Paul Krugman)在1995年写道:

p12.original: It is a late-twentieth-century conceit that we invented the global economy just yesterday. In fact, world markets achieved an impressive degree of integration during the second half of the nineteenth century. Indeed, if one wants a specific date for the beginning of a truly global economy, one might well choose 1869, the year in which both the Suez Canal and the Union Pacific railroad were completed. By the eve of the First World War steamships and railroads had created markets for standardized commodities, like wheat and wool, that were fully global in their reach. Even the global flow of information was better than modern observers, focused on electronic technology, tend to realize: the first submarine telegraph cable was laid under the Atlantic in 1858, and by 1900 all of the world’s major economic regions could effectively communicate instantaneously.
p12.zh: 我们昨天发明了全球经济,这是20世纪晚期的自以为是。 事实上,世界市场在19世纪下半叶实现了令人印象深刻的一体化。 的确,如果人们想要一个开始真正全球经济的具体日期,人们很可能选择1869年,即苏伊士运河和联合太平洋铁路完成的一年。到了第一次世界大战前夕,蒸汽船和铁路已经为标准化商品创造了市场,如小麦和羊毛,这些商品完全覆盖全球. 甚至全球的信息流动都比以电子技术为主的现代观察者要好,往往会意识到:1858年在大西洋下铺设了第一部潜艇电报电报电报线,到1900年,世界所有主要经济区域都能有效地瞬间通信.

p13.original: This first wave of globalization crashed to a halt early in the twentieth century. World War I severed many economic connections. During the Great Depression of the 1930s, many nations misguidedly tried to fix their own economies by reducing foreign trade with others. World War II further hindered international trade. Global flows of goods and financial capital were rebuilt only slowly after World War II. It was not until the early 1980s that global economic forces again became as important, relative to the size of the world economy, as they were before World War I.
p13.zh: 第一次全球化浪潮在20世纪初陷入停顿。第一次世界大战切断了许多经济联系. 在1930年代的大萧条时期,许多国家错误地试图通过减少与其他国家的对外贸易来修补自己的经济. 二战进一步阻碍了国际贸易. 二战结束后,全球物资和金融资本的流通才缓慢重建. 直到1980年代初期,全球经济力量才再次变得与第一次世界大战之前的世界经济规模一样重要。

p15.original: The American statesman Benjamin Franklin (1706–1790) once wrote: “No nation was ever ruined by trade.” Many economists would express their attitudes toward international trade in an even more positive manner. The evidence that international trade confers overall benefits on economies is pretty strong. Trade has accompanied economic growth in the United States and around the world. Many of the national economies that have shown the most rapid growth in the last several decades—for example, Japan, South Korea, China, and India—have done so by dramatically orienting their economies toward international trade. There is no modern example of a country that has shut itself off from world trade and yet prospered. To understand the benefits of trade, or why we trade in the first place, we need to understand the concepts of comparative and absolute advantage.
p15.zh: 美国政治家本杰明·富兰克林(1706–1790)曾写道 : “ 没有一个国家被贸易破坏过。 ”许多经济学家会以更积极的方式表达他们对国际贸易的态度。国际贸易给各经济体带来总体利益的证据相当有力。贸易伴随着美国和全世界的经济增长。 过去几十年中增长最快的许多国家经济体,例如日本、韩国、中国和印度,都通过大幅度调整其经济方向,将其经济转向国际贸易来实现增长。没有任何现代的例子表明一个国家已经关闭了与世界贸易的联系,但却实现了繁荣。 为了了解贸易的好处,或者我们首先贸易的原因,我们需要了解比较优势和绝对优势的概念。

p16.original: In 1817, David Ricardo, a businessman, economist, and member of the British Parliament, wrote a treatise called On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation. In this treatise, Ricardo argued that specialization and free trade benefit all trading partners, even those that may be relatively inefficient. To see what he meant, we must be able to distinguish between absolute and comparative advantage.
p16.zh: 1817年,商人,经济学家,英国国会议员大卫·里卡多(David Ricardo)撰写了一篇名为"关于政治经济和税收的原则"的论文. 在这份论文中,Ricardo认为,专业化和自由贸易有利于所有贸易伙伴,即使是那些可能效率相对较低的贸易伙伴。 为了了解他的意思,我们必须能够区分绝对优势和比较优势。

p17.original: A country has an absolute advantage over another country in producing a good if it can produce more of that good. Absolute advantage can be the result of a country’s having more resources, having more productive resources, or its natural endowment. For example, extracting oil in Saudi Arabia is pretty much just a matter of “drilling a hole.” Producing oil in other countries can require considerable exploration and costly technologies for drilling and extraction—if they have any oil at all. The United States has some of the richest farmland in the world, making it easier to grow corn and wheat than in many other countries. Guatemala and Colombia have climates especially suited for growing coffee. Chile and Zambia have some of the world’s richest copper mines. As some have argued, “geography is destiny.” Chile will provide copper and Guatemala will produce coffee, and they will trade. When each country has a product others need and it can produce it with fewer resources in one country than in another, then it is easy to imagine all parties benefitting from trade. However, thinking about trade just in terms of geography and absolute advantage is incomplete. Trade really occurs because of comparative advantage.
p17.zh: 一个国家如果能够生产更多的商品,在生产商品方面比另一个国家拥有绝对优势。绝对优势可能是一国拥有更多资源、生产资源或自然财富的结果。 例如,在沙特阿拉伯开采石油几乎只是“钻洞 ” 。 在其他国家生产石油可能需要大量的勘探和昂贵的钻探技术,如果它们有石油的话。 美国拥有世界上一些最富饶的农田,因此比其他许多国家更容易种植玉米和小麦. 危地马拉和哥伦比亚的气候特别适合种植咖啡。 智利和赞比亚拥有世界上一些最丰富的铜矿。 正如有些人所说 , “ 地理是命运。 ”智利将提供铜,危地马拉将生产咖啡,并将进行贸易。 当每个国家都有其他国家需要的产品,而且一国的资源比另一国少,因此很容易想象所有各方都能从贸易中获益。 然而,仅仅从地理和绝对优势的角度来考虑贸易是不完整的。贸易之所以出现,真正是因为比较优势。

p18.original: Recall from the chapter Choice in a World of Scarcity that a country has a comparative advantage when it can produce a good at a lower cost in terms of other goods. The question each country or company should be asking when it trades is this: “What do we give up to produce this good?” It should be no surprise that the concept of comparative advantage is based on this idea of opportunity cost from Choice in a World of Scarcity. For example, if Zambia focuses its resources on producing copper, it cannot use its labor, land and financial resources to produce other goods such as corn. As a result, Zambia gives up the opportunity to produce corn. How do we quantify the cost in terms of other goods? Simplify the problem and assume that Zambia just needs labor to produce copper and corn. The companies that produce either copper or corn tell you that it takes two hours to mine a ton of copper and one hour to harvest a bushel of corn. This means the opportunity cost of producing a ton of copper is two bushels of corn. The next section develops absolute and comparative advantage in greater detail and relates them to trade.
p18.zh: 从一章中回顾,在缺乏世界的选择中,一个国家如果能够以较低成本在其他商品上生产商品,就具有比较优势。每个国家或公司在交易时都应该问的问题是:“我们为了生产这种商品而放弃什么?” 比较优势的概念是基于“在匮乏的世界中选择机会的代价”这一理念,这不足为奇。 例如,如果赞比亚将其资源集中用于生产铜,它就不能利用其劳动力、土地和财政资源来生产其他商品,如玉米。 因此,赞比亚放弃了生产玉米的机会。 我们如何量化其他商品的成本?简化问题,并假定赞比亚只需要劳动来生产铜和玉米。生产铜或玉米的公司告诉你,开采一吨铜需要两个小时,收获一束玉米需要一个小时。 这意味着生产一吨铜的机会成本是玉米的两种灌木.下一节将更详细地发展绝对和比较优势,并将其与贸易联系起来。

p20.original: A Numerical Example of Absolute and Comparative Advantage
p20.zh: 绝对和比较优势的数字示例

p21.original: Consider a hypothetical world with two countries, Saudi Arabia and the United States, and two products, oil and corn. Further assume that consumers in both countries desire both these goods. These goods are homogeneous, meaning that consumers/producers cannot differentiate between corn or oil from either country. There is only one resource available in both countries, labor hours. Saudi Arabia can produce oil with fewer resources, while the United States can produce corn with fewer resources.  illustrates the advantages of the two countries, expressed in terms of how many hours it takes to produce one unit of each good.
p21.zh: 考虑一个假想的世界,有两个国家,沙特阿拉伯和美国,还有两种产品,石油和玉米.进一步假定两国的消费者都渴望这两种商品。 这些商品是同质的,即消费者/生产者不能区分来自任何国家的玉米或石油。两国只有一种资源,即劳动时数。沙特阿拉伯可以用更少的资源生产石油,而美国可以用更少的资源生产玉米. 说明两国的优势,以每件商品生产一个单位需要多少时间来表示.

p22.original: How Many Hours It Takes to Produce Oil and Corn
p22.zh: 生产石油和玉米需要多少小时

p32.original: In , Saudi Arabia has an absolute advantage in producing oil because it only takes an hour to produce a barrel of oil compared to two hours in the United States. The United States has an absolute advantage in producing corn.
p32.zh: 沙特阿拉伯在生产石油方面有绝对优势,因为生产一桶石油只需要一个小时,而美国只有两个小时。 美国在生产玉米方面拥有绝对优势.

p33.original: To simplify, let’s say that Saudi Arabia and the United States each have 100 worker hours (see ).  illustrates what each country is capable of producing on its own using a production possibility frontier (PPF) graph. Recall from Choice in a World of Scarcity that the production possibilities frontier shows the maximum amount that each country can produce given its limited resources, in this case workers, and its level of technology.
p33.zh: 简而言之,我们假设沙特阿拉伯和美国各有100个工人小时(参见 ) 。 说明每个国家利用生产可能性前沿图(PPF)能够自行生产什么。 从 " 在匮乏的世界中作出选择 " 中回顾,生产可能性的前沿表明,鉴于各国资源有限,例如工人,以及技术水平,每个国家能够生产的最大数量。

p36.zh: 使用100个工人小时的石油生产(桶)

p48.original: Arguably Saudi and U.S. consumers desire both oil and corn to live. Let’s say that before trade occurs, both countries produce and consume at point C or C'. Thus, before trade, the Saudi Arabian economy will devote 60 worker hours to produce oil, as  shows. Given the information in , this choice implies that it produces/consumes 60 barrels of oil. With the remaining 40 worker hours, since it needs four hours to produce a bushel of corn, it can produce only 10 bushels. To be at point C', the U.S. economy devotes 40 worker hours to produce 20 barrels of oil and it can allocate the remaining worker hours to produce 60 bushels of corn.
p48.zh: 可以说沙特和美国的消费者都渴望石油和玉米都能够生存.两国在C点或C点生产消费。 因此,如所示,在贸易之前,沙特阿拉伯经济将花60个工人小时生产石油。 鉴于其中的信息,这一选择意味着它生产/消耗60桶石油。剩下的40个工时,由于生产一整束玉米需要4小时,因此只能生产10根灌木.到了C点,美国经济用40个工人小时生产20桶石油,它可以分配剩下的工人小时生产60只灌木的玉米.

p62.original: The slope of the production possibility frontier illustrates the opportunity cost of producing oil in terms of corn. Using all its resources, the United States can produce 50 barrels of oil or 100 bushels of corn; therefore, the opportunity cost of one barrel of oil is two bushels of corn—or the slope is 1/2. Thus, in the U.S. production possibility frontier graph, every increase in oil production of one barrel implies a decrease of two bushels of corn. Saudi Arabia can produce 100 barrels of oil or 25 bushels of corn. The opportunity cost of producing one barrel of oil is the loss of 1/4 of a bushel of corn that Saudi workers could otherwise have produced. In terms of corn, notice that Saudi Arabia gives up the least to produce a barrel of oil.  summarizes these calculations.
p62.zh: 生产可能性的坡度前沿表明,玉米生产石油的机会成本。 美国利用其所有资源,可以生产50桶石油或100根玉米;因此,一桶石油的机会成本是两桶玉米——或者坡度是1/2. 因此,在美国生产可能性前沿图中,每增加一桶油的石油产量,就意味着玉米的两只灌木丛减少。沙特阿拉伯可生产100桶石油或25根玉米。生产一桶石油的机会成本是沙特工人本来可以生产的1/4毛毛的玉米损失。 在玉米方面,注意到沙特阿拉伯放弃了生产一桶石油的最低程度。

p65.zh: 一个单位的机会成本——石油(按玉米计算)

p66.zh: 一个单位的机会成本——玉米(石油方面)

p73.original: Again recall that we defined comparative advantage as the opportunity cost of producing goods. Since Saudi Arabia gives up the least to produce a barrel of oil, (14 <  < 2 in  in ) it has a comparative advantage in oil production. The United States gives up the least to produce a bushel of corn, so it has a comparative advantage in corn production.
p73.zh: 我们再次回顾,我们把比较优势界定为生产商品的机会成本。 由于沙特阿拉伯放弃生产一桶石油最少(14 < 2 in),它在石油生产方面具有比较优势。 美国放弃了生产一丁点玉米,因此在玉米生产上具有比较优势.

p74.original: In this example, there is symmetry between absolute and comparative advantage. Saudi Arabia needs fewer worker hours to produce oil (absolute advantage, see ), and also gives up the least in terms of other goods to produce oil (comparative advantage, see ). Such symmetry is not always the case, as we will show after we have discussed gains from trade fully, but first, read the following Clear It Up feature to make sure you understand why the PPF line in the graphs is straight.
p74.zh: 在这个例子中,绝对优势和比较优势是对称的.沙特阿拉伯生产石油需要较少的工人工时(绝对优势,见......),在生产石油的其他商品方面也放弃最少的工人工时(比较优势,见......)。 这种对称性并非总是如此,在我们充分讨论贸易收益之后,我们将表明这一点,但首先,读一下以下的“澄清”特征,以确保你理解为什么图表中的PPF线是直线的。

p75.original: Can a production possibility frontier be straight?
p75.zh: 一个生产可能性的前沿能否是直线的?

p76.original: When you first met the production possibility frontier (PPF) in the chapter on Choice in a World of Scarcity we drew it with an outward-bending shape. This shape illustrated that as we transferred inputs from producing one good to another—like from education to health services—there were increasing opportunity costs. In the examples in this chapter, we draw the PPFs as straight lines, which means that opportunity costs are constant. When we transfer a marginal unit of labor away from growing corn and toward producing oil, the decline in the quantity of corn and the increase in the quantity of oil is always the same. In reality this is possible only if the contribution of additional workers to output did not change as the scale of production changed. The linear production possibilities frontier is a less realistic model, but a straight line simplifies calculations. It also illustrates economic themes like absolute and comparative advantage just as clearly.
p76.zh: 当你第一次遇到生产可能性前沿(PPF)的时候, 我们画的是一个外向的形状。 这种形式表明,当我们把投入从生产一种商品转移到另一种商品时,例如从教育转移到保健服务时,机会成本在增加。 在本章中的例子中,我们绘制的PPF是直线的,这意味着机会成本是不变的. 当我们将一个边际劳动力单位从种植玉米转移到生产石油时,玉米数量的下降和石油数量的增加总是一样。 实际上,只有在增加的工人对产出的贡献没有随着生产规模的改变而改变的情况下,才有可能做到这一点。线性生产可能性前沿是一个不太现实的模型,但直线简化了计算. 它还同样清楚地说明了经济主题,如绝对和比较优势。

p78.original:
Consider the trading positions of the United States and Saudi Arabia after they have specialized and traded. Before trade, Saudi Arabia produces/consumes 60 barrels of oil and 10 bushels of corn. The United States produces/consumes 20 barrels of oil and 60 bushels of corn. Given their current production levels, if the United States can trade an amount of corn fewer than 60 bushels and receive in exchange an amount of oil greater than 20 barrels, it will gain from trade. With trade, the United States can consume more of both goods than it did without specialization and trade. (Recall that the chapter
Welcome to Economics! defined specialization as it applies to workers and firms. Economists also use specialization to describe the occurrence when a country shifts resources to focus on producing a good that offers comparative advantage.) Similarly, if Saudi Arabia can trade an amount of oil less than 60 barrels and receive in exchange an amount of corn greater than 10 bushels, it will have more of both goods than it did before specialization and trade.  illustrates the range of trades that would benefit both sides.

p86.original: The underlying reason why trade benefits both sides is rooted in the concept of opportunity cost, as the following Clear It Up feature explains. p145.original: What Happens When a Country Has an Absolute Advantage in All Goods

p146.original: What happens to the possibilities for trade if one country has an absolute advantage in everything? This is typical for high-income countries that often have well-educated workers, technologically advanced equipment, and the most up-to-date production processes. These high-income countries can produce all products with fewer resources than a low-income country. If the high-income country is more productive across the board, will there still be gains from trade? Good students of Ricardo understand that trade is about mutually beneficial exchange. Even when one country has an absolute advantage in all products, trade can still benefit both sides. This is because gains from trade come from specializing in one’s comparative advantage.
p146.zh: 如果一个国家在一切方面都具有绝对优势,贸易的可能性会如何?这对于收入高的国家来说是典型的,这些国家往往拥有受过良好教育的工人、技术先进的设备以及最新的生产工艺。 这些高收入国家可以生产资源少于低收入国家的所有产品。 如果高收入国家整体生产力提高,贸易是否还有收益?里卡多的好学生们明白贸易是互利的交换. 即使一个国家在所有产品上拥有绝对优势,贸易仍然可以使双方受益.这是因为贸易收益来自专门发挥比较优势。

p159.original: Absolute advantage simply compares the productivity of a worker between countries. It answers the question, “How many inputs do I need to produce shoes in Mexico?” Comparative advantage asks this same question slightly differently. Instead of comparing how many workers it takes to produce a good, it asks, “How much am I giving up to produce this good in this country?” Another way of looking at this is that comparative advantage identifies the good for which the producer’s absolute advantage is relatively larger, or where the producer’s absolute productivity disadvantage is relatively smaller. The United States can produce 1,000 shoes with four-fifths as many workers as Mexico (four versus five), but it can produce 1,000 refrigerators with only one-quarter as many workers (one versus four). So, the comparative advantage of the United States, where its absolute productivity advantage is relatively greatest, lies with refrigerators, and Mexico’s comparative advantage, where its absolute productivity disadvantage is least, is in the production of shoes.
p159.zh: 绝对优势只是比较了国家之间工人的生产力。 它回答了“我需要多少投入才能在墨西哥生产鞋?” 的这个问题。 比较优势对这个问题的质疑略有不同。与其比较生产商品需要多少工人,它问道,“我为了生产这种商品要放弃多少? ” 另一种观点是,比较优势确定了生产者的绝对优势相对较大,或者生产者的绝对生产力劣势相对较小的有利条件。 美国可以生产1000双鞋,工人数量与墨西哥的五分之四(四对五),但可以生产1000个冰箱,工人数量只有四分之一(一对四). 因此,美国绝对生产力优势相对最大的比较优势在于冰箱,而墨西哥绝对生产力劣势最小的比较优势在于鞋的生产.

p192.original: Continuing with this scenario, suppose that each country transfers some amount of labor toward its area of comparative advantage. For example, the United States transfers six workers away from shoes and toward producing refrigerators. As a result, U.S. production of shoes decreases by 1,500 units (6/4 × 1,000), while its production of refrigerators increases by 6,000 (that is, 6/1 × 1,000). Mexico also moves production toward its area of comparative advantage, transferring 10 workers away from refrigerators and toward production of shoes. As a result, production of refrigerators in Mexico falls by 2,500 (10/4 × 1,000), but production of shoes increases by 2,000 pairs (10/5 × 1,000). Notice that when both countries shift production toward each of their comparative advantages (what they are relatively better at), their combined production of both goods rises, as shown in . The reduction of shoe production by 1,500 pairs in the United States is more than offset by the gain of 2,000 pairs of shoes in Mexico, while the reduction of 2,500 refrigerators in Mexico is more than offset by the additional 6,000 refrigerators produced in the United States.
p192.zh: 继续这种设想,假设每个国家将一定的劳动力转移到其比较优势领域。 例如,美国将6名工人从鞋中调走,转而生产冰箱。 因此,美国鞋的生产减少了1500套(6/4×1000),而其冰箱的生产则增加了6000套(即6/1×1000). 墨西哥还将生产转向其相对优势领域,将10名工人从冰箱中转移,转向生产鞋类。 因此,墨西哥的冰箱产量下降了2500(10/4×1000),但鞋类产量增加了2000对(10/5×1000).注意当两国将生产转向各自的相对优势(它们相对较好的优势)时,它们两种商品的合并生产就会上升,如......所示。 美国鞋产量减少1500双,墨西哥的2000双鞋增产抵消了以上,而墨西哥的2500台冰箱减产抵消了以上,美国生产的6000台冰箱增产抵消以上.

p193.original: Shifting Production Toward Comparative Advantage Raises Total Output
p193.zh: 将生产转向比较优势,提高总产出

p206.original: This numerical example illustrates the remarkable insight of comparative advantage: even when one country has an absolute advantage in all goods and another country has an absolute disadvantage in all goods, both countries can still benefit from trade. Even though the United States has an absolute advantage in producing both refrigerators and shoes, it makes economic sense for it to specialize in the good for which it has a comparative advantage. The United States will export refrigerators and in return import shoes.
p206.zh: 这一数字例子说明了比较优势的显著意义:即使一个国家在所有货物上拥有绝对优势,而另一个国家在所有货物上拥有绝对劣势,两国仍然可以从贸易中获益。 尽管美国在生产冰箱和鞋子方面都具有绝对优势,但美国专门从事其具有比较优势的利得却具有经济意义. 美国将出口冰箱和回馈进口鞋。

p207.original: How Opportunity Cost Sets the Boundaries of Trade
p207.zh: 机会成本如何确定贸易的界限

p208.original: This example shows that both parties can benefit from specializing in their comparative advantages and trading. By using the opportunity costs in this example, it is possible to identify the range of possible trades that would benefit each country.
p208.zh: 这一例子表明,双方都可以从各自的比较优势和贸易方面获得好处。 通过利用这一例子中的机会成本,可以确定可能有利于每个国家的贸易范围。

p209.original: Mexico started out, before specialization and trade, producing 4,000 pairs of shoes and 5,000 refrigerators (see  and ). Then, in the numerical example given, Mexico shifted production toward its comparative advantage and produced 6,000 pairs of shoes but only 2,500 refrigerators. Thus, if Mexico can export no more than 2,000 pairs of shoes (giving up 2,000 pairs of shoes) in exchange for imports of at least 2,500 refrigerators (a gain of 2,500 refrigerators), it will be able to consume more of both goods than before trade. Mexico will be unambiguously better off. Conversely, the United States started off, before specialization and trade, producing 5,000 pairs of shoes and 20,000 refrigerators. In the example, it then shifted production toward its comparative advantage, producing only 3,500 shoes but 26,000 refrigerators. If the United States can export no more than 6,000 refrigerators in exchange for imports of at least 1,500 pairs of shoes, it will be able to consume more of both goods and will be unambiguously better off.
p209.zh: 墨西哥在专业化和贸易之前开始生产4 000双鞋和5 000个冰箱(见和)。 然后,在给出的数字例子中,墨西哥将生产转向其比较优势,生产了6 000双鞋,但只有2 500台冰箱。 因此,如果墨西哥能够出口不超过2 000双鞋(赠送2 000双鞋),以换取至少2 500个冰箱的进口(增加2 500个冰箱),那么,墨西哥将比贸易前消费更多的这两种货物。 墨西哥无疑会更好。 相反,美国在专业化和贸易之前就已开始生产5 000双鞋和20 000台冰箱。举例来说,它随后将生产转向其比较优势,只生产3,500双鞋,但生产了26,000台冰箱。 如果美国能够出口不超过6 000台冰箱,以换取至少1 500双鞋的进口,它就能消耗更多的这两类货物,并且无疑会更好。

p210.original: The range of trades that can benefit both nations is shown in . For example, a trade where the U.S. exports 4,000 refrigerators to Mexico in exchange for 1,800 pairs of shoes would benefit both sides, in the sense that both countries would be able to consume more of both goods than in a world without trade.
p210.zh: 能够使两国受益的贸易范围见以下各段。 例如,美国向墨西哥出口4000台冰箱以换取1800双鞋的贸易,将有利于双方,因为两国都能消费更多的两种商品,而不是在没有贸易的世界中.

p211.original: The Range of Trades That Benefit Both the United States and Mexico
p211.zh: 使美国和墨西哥都受益的贸易范围

p212.zh: 美国经济在专业化之后,如果:

p213.original: The Mexican economy, after specialization, will benefit if it:
p213.zh: 墨西哥经济在专业化之后,如果:

p216.original: Imports at least 1,500 pairs of shoes

p217.original: Exports no more than 2,000 pairs of shoes

p218.original: Trade allows each country to take advantage of lower opportunity costs in the other country. If Mexico wants to produce more refrigerators without trade, it must face its domestic opportunity costs and reduce shoe production. If Mexico, instead, produces more shoes and then trades for refrigerators made in the United States, where the opportunity cost of producing refrigerators is lower, Mexico can in effect take advantage of the lower opportunity cost of refrigerators in the United States. Conversely, when the United States specializes in its comparative advantage of refrigerator production and trades for shoes produced in Mexico, international trade allows the United States to take advantage of the lower opportunity cost of shoe production in Mexico.
p218.zh: 贸易允许每个国家利用对方国家较低的机会成本。 如果墨西哥想要生产更多的冰箱,而不进行贸易,它就必须面对国内的机会成本,减少鞋的生产. 如果墨西哥生产更多的鞋子,然后在美国生产冰箱,而美国生产冰箱的机会成本较低,墨西哥实际上可以利用美国冰箱的机会成本较低。 相反,当美国专门发挥墨西哥生产的冰箱生产和鞋类贸易的比较优势时,国际贸易允许美国利用墨西哥鞋类生产的机会成本较低.

p219.original: The theory of comparative advantage explains why countries trade: they have different comparative advantages. It shows that the gains from international trade result from pursuing comparative advantage and producing at a lower opportunity cost. The following Work It Out feature shows how to calculate absolute and comparative advantage and the way to apply them to a country’s production.
p219.zh: 比较优势理论解释了各国贸易的原因:它们具有不同的比较优势。 它表明,国际贸易的收益来自追求比较优势和低机会成本的生产。 以下的“工作”特征说明如何计算绝对和比较优势,以及如何将这些优势应用于一个国家的生产。

p220.zh: 计算绝对优势和比较优势

p221.original: In Canada a worker can produce 20 barrels of oil or 40 tons of lumber. In Venezuela, a worker can produce 60 barrels of oil or 30 tons of lumber.
p221.zh: 在加拿大,工人可以生产20桶石油或40吨木材。 在委内瑞拉,工人可以生产60桶石油或30吨木材。

p234.original: Who has the absolute advantage in the production of oil or lumber? How can you tell?
p234.zh: 谁在生产石油或木材方面有绝对优势? 你怎么看出来?

p235.original: Which country has a comparative advantage in the production of oil?
p235.zh: 哪个国家在石油生产方面具有比较优势?

p236.original: Which country has a comparative advantage in producing lumber?
p236.zh: 哪个国家在木材生产方面具有相对优势?

p237.original: In this example, is absolute advantage the same as comparative advantage, or not?
p237.zh: 在这个例子中,绝对优势是否与比较优势相同?

p238.original: In what product should Canada specialize? In what product should Venezuela specialize?
p238.zh: 加拿大应该专门生产哪一种产品?委内瑞拉应该专门生产哪些产品?

p240.original: Step 2. To calculate absolute advantage, look at the larger of the numbers for each product. One worker in Canada can produce more lumber (40 tons versus 30 tons), so Canada has the absolute advantage in lumber. One worker in Venezuela can produce 60 barrels of oil compared to a worker in Canada who can produce only 20.
p240.zh: 步骤二. 为了计算绝对优势,看看每种产品中数量越大. 加拿大的一位工人可以生产更多的木材(40吨对30吨),因此加拿大在木材方面拥有绝对优势.委内瑞拉有一名工人可以生产60桶石油,而加拿大一名工人只能生产20桶石油。

p241.original: Step 3. To calculate comparative advantage, find the opportunity cost of producing one barrel of oil in both countries. The country with the lowest opportunity cost has the comparative advantage. With the same labor time, Canada can produce either 20 barrels of oil or 40 tons of lumber. So in effect, 20 barrels of oil is equivalent to 40 tons of lumber: 20 oil = 40 lumber. Divide both sides of the equation by 20 to calculate the opportunity cost of one barrel of oil in Canada. 20/20 oil = 40/20 lumber. 1 oil = 2 lumber. To produce one additional barrel of oil in Canada has an opportunity cost of 2 lumber. Calculate the same way for Venezuela: 60 oil = 30 lumber. Divide both sides of the equation by 60. One oil in Venezuela has an opportunity cost of 1/2 lumber. Because 1/2 lumber < 2 lumber, Venezuela has the comparative advantage in producing oil.
p241.zh: 步骤3。 为了计算比较优势,找出两国生产一桶石油的机会成本。机会成本最低的国家具有比较优势。同样的劳动时间,加拿大可以生产20桶石油或40吨木材. 因此实际上,20桶石油相当于40吨的木材:20个石油=40个木材.将方程式的两边除以20,以计算加拿大一桶石油的机会成本。20/20 石油 = 40/20 木材。1 油 = 2 木材.在加拿大再生产一桶石油的机会成本为2个木材。委内瑞拉的计算方式相同:60石油=30木材。方程的两边除以60.委内瑞拉的1种石油的机会成本为1/2木材。 由于1/2个木材 < 2个木材,委内瑞拉在生产石油方面具有比较优势。

p242.original: Step 4. Calculate the opportunity cost of one lumber by reversing the numbers, with lumber on the left side of the equation. In Canada, 40 lumber is equivalent in labor time to 20 barrels of oil: 40 lumber = 20 oil. Divide each side of the equation by 40. The opportunity cost of one lumber is 1/2 oil. In Venezuela, the equivalent labor time will produce 30 lumber or 60 oil: 30 lumber = 60 oil. Divide each side by 30. One lumber has an opportunity cost of two oil. Canada has the lower opportunity cost in producing lumber.
p242.zh: 步骤4。 通过倒转数字计算一个木材的机会成本,其中木材位于方程的左侧.在加拿大,40个木材在劳动时间上相当于20桶石油:40个木材=20个石油.方程每边除以40. 一个木材的机会成本是1/2油。 在委内瑞拉,相同的劳动时间将生产30个木材或60个石油:30个木材=60个石油。 每边除以30. 一个木材有两种石油的机会成本。 加拿大生产木材的机会成本较低。

p243.original: Step 5. In this example, absolute advantage is the same as comparative advantage. Canada has the absolute and comparative advantage in lumber; Venezuela has the absolute and comparative advantage in oil.
p243.zh: 步骤5。 在这个例子中,绝对优势与比较优势相同. 加拿大在木材方面拥有绝对和相对优势;委内瑞拉在石油方面拥有绝对和相对优势。

p244.original: Step 6. Canada should specialize in the commodity for which it has a relative lower opportunity cost, which is lumber, and Venezuela should specialize in oil. Canada will be exporting lumber and importing oil, and Venezuela will be exporting oil and importing lumber.
p244.zh: 步骤6。 加拿大应专门从事其机会成本相对较低的商品,即木材,委内瑞拉应专门从事石油。 加拿大将出口木材和进口石油,委内瑞拉将出口石油和进口木材。

p246.original: To build an intuitive understanding of how comparative advantage can benefit all parties, set aside examples that involve national economies for a moment and consider the situation of a group of friends who decide to go camping together. The six friends have a wide range of skills and experiences, but one person in particular, Jethro, has done lots of camping before and is also a great athlete. Jethro has an absolute advantage in all aspects of camping: he is faster at carrying a backpack, gathering firewood, paddling a canoe, setting up tents, making a meal, and washing up. So here is the question: Because Jethro has an absolute productivity advantage in everything, should he do all the work?
p246.zh: 为了直观地了解比较优势如何能惠及所有各方,暂举一些涉及国民经济的例子,并审议一组决定一起露营的朋友的情况。 这六位朋友拥有广泛的技能和经验,但其中特别有一人杰思罗在之前做过很多露营,同时也是一名优秀的运动员. 杰思罗在露营的各个方面都有着绝对的优势:他更快地携带背包,拾柴,划划舟,搭帐篷,做饭,洗碗.问题就在这里:因为杰思罗在一切方面都有绝对的生产力优势,他应该做所有的工作吗?

p247.original: Of course not! Even if Jethro is willing to work like a mule while everyone else sits around, he, like all mortals, only has 24 hours in a day. If everyone sits around and waits for Jethro to do everything, not only will Jethro be an unhappy camper, but there will not be much output for his group of six friends to consume. The theory of comparative advantage suggests that everyone will benefit if they figure out their areas of comparative advantage—that is, the area of camping where their productivity disadvantage is least, compared to Jethro. For example, it may be that Jethro is 80% faster at building fires and cooking meals than anyone else, but only 20% faster at gathering firewood and 10% faster at setting up tents. In that case, Jethro should focus on building fires and making meals, and others should attend to the other tasks, each according to where their productivity disadvantage is smallest. If the campers coordinate their efforts according to comparative advantage, they can all gain.
p247.zh: 当然不是! 即使杰思罗愿意像骡子一样工作,而其他人却坐在身边,他和所有凡人一样,一天只有24小时的时间. 如果每个人都坐着等待杰思罗做一切事情,那么杰思罗不仅会是一个不愉快的露营者,而且他的六位朋友组的消耗量也不会太多.比较优势理论表明,如果找出自己比较优势的领域,即与Jethro相比,在生产力劣势最小的营地,每个人都会受益。 例如,Jethro在建火和做饭方面比其他人快80%,但在收集柴火方面却快20%,在搭帐篷方面快10%。 在这种情况下,Jethro应该专注于建火和做饭,其他人应该照顾其他任务,每个任务根据其生产力劣势最小的地方. 如果露营者根据比较优势协调他们的努力,他们都能够受益.

p249.original: Even when a country has high levels of productivity in all goods, it can still benefit from trade. Gains from trade come about as a result of comparative advantage. By specializing in a good that it gives up the least to produce, a country can produce more and offer that additional output for sale. If other countries specialize in the area of their comparative advantage as well and trade, the highly productive country is able to benefit from a lower opportunity cost of production in other countries.
p249.zh: 即使一个国家在所有商品方面都具有高水平的生产力,它仍然能够从贸易中受益。贸易收益来自比较优势。一个国家通过专门生产它放弃最少的商品,可以生产更多的商品,并提供额外产出供销售。 如果其他国家也专门从事其比较优势和贸易领域,高生产力国家能够受益于其他国家较低的生产机会成本。

p251.original: In Germany it takes three workers to make one television and four workers to make one video camera. In Poland it takes six workers to make one television and 12 workers to make one video camera.
p251.zh: 在德国,制造一台电视机需要3名工人,制造一台录像机需要4名工人。 在波兰,制作一台电视机需要6名工人,制作一台录像机需要12名工人。

p252.original: Who has the absolute advantage in the production of televisions? Who has the absolute advantage in the production of video cameras? How can you tell?
p252.zh: 谁在电视的制作上拥有绝对优势?. 谁在摄像头的制作中拥有绝对优势?. 你怎么看出来?

p253.original: Calculate the opportunity cost of producing one additional television set in Germany and in Poland. (Your calculation may involve fractions, which is fine.) Which country has a comparative advantage in the production of televisions?
p253.zh: 计算在德国和波兰再生产一台电视机的机会成本。(你的计算可能涉及分数,这很好。 )哪个国家在电视制作方面有相对优势?

p254.original: Calculate the opportunity cost of producing one video camera in Germany and in Poland. Which country has a comparative advantage in the production of video cameras?
p254.zh: 计算在德国和波兰生产一台摄像机的机会成本。哪个国家在录像机生产方面有相对优势?

p255.original: In this example, is absolute advantage the same as comparative advantage, or not?
p255.zh: 在这个例子中,绝对优势是否与比较优势相同?

p256.original: In what product should Germany specialize? In what product should Poland specialize?
p256.zh: 德国应该专门生产哪种产品? 波兰应该专门生产哪一种产品?

p257.original: In Germany, it takes fewer workers to make either a television or a video camera. Germany has an absolute advantage in the production of both goods.
p257.zh: 在德国,制作电视或录像机需要较少的工人. 德国在这两种商品的生产上都具有绝对优势.

p258.original: Producing an additional television in Germany requires three workers. Shifting those three German workers will reduce video camera production by 3/4 of a camera. Producing an additional television set in Poland requires six workers, and shifting those workers from the other good reduces output of video cameras by 6/12 of a camera, or 1/2. Thus, the opportunity cost of producing televisions is lower in Poland, so Poland has the comparative advantage in the production of televisions. Note: Do not let the fractions like 3/4 of a camera or 1/2 of a video camera bother you. If either country was to expand television production by a significant amount—that is, lots more than one unit—then we will be talking about whole cameras and not fractional ones. You can also spot this conclusion by noticing that Poland’s absolute disadvantage is relatively lower in televisions, because Poland needs twice as many workers to produce a television but three times as many to produce a video camera, so the product with the relatively lower absolute disadvantage is Poland’s comparative advantage.
p258.zh: 在德国生产额外的电视需要三名工人。转移这三名德国工人 将减少摄像头生产 3/4的摄像头。 在波兰再生产一台电视机需要6名工人,而将这些工人从其他好设备中调走,则减少了摄像头的6/12或1/2的摄像头输出。 因此,波兰制作电视机的机会成本较低,因此波兰在电视机制作方面拥有比较优势.注意: 不要让相机的3/4或相机的1/2. 如果任何国家都把电视制作量扩大很多,也就是说,超过一个单位的数量,那么我们将谈论的是整台摄像机,而不是零星的摄像机。 你也可以通过注意到波兰的绝对劣势在电视上相对较低来发现这个结论,因为波兰生产电视需要两倍的工人,而生产录像机需要三倍的工人,因此具有相对较低绝对劣势的产品是波兰的比较优势.

p259.original: Producing a video camera in Germany requires four workers, and shifting those four workers away from television production has an opportunity cost of 4/3 television sets. Producing a video camera in Poland requires 12 workers, and shifting those 12 workers away from television production has an opportunity cost of two television sets. Thus, the opportunity cost of producing video cameras is lower in Germany, and video cameras will be Germany’s comparative advantage.
p259.zh: 在德国生产一台录像机需要4名工人,将这4名工人从电视制作中调走,其机会成本为4/3台电视机。 在波兰生产一台录像机需要12名工人,而将这12名工人从电视制作中转移出去则需要两台电视机的机会成本。 因此,在德国,摄像头生产的机会成本较低,而摄像头将是德国的比较优势.

p260.original: In this example, absolute advantage differs from comparative advantage. Germany has the absolute advantage in the production of both goods, but Poland has a comparative advantage in the production of televisions.
p260.zh: 在这个例子中,绝对优势与比较优势不同. 德国在这两种商品的生产上都具有绝对优势,但波兰在电视机的生产上却具有比较优势.

p261.original: Germany should specialize, at least to some extent, in the production of video cameras, export video cameras, and import televisions. Conversely, Poland should specialize, at least to some extent, in the production of televisions, export televisions, and import video cameras.
p261.zh: 德国应至少在某种程度上专门生产摄像机、出口摄像机和进口电视。 相反,波兰应至少在某种程度上专门生产电视、出口电视和进口录像机。

p263.original: Is it possible to have a comparative advantage in the production of a good but not to have an absolute advantage? Explain.
p263.zh: 能否在生产商品方面拥有比较优势,但不能拥有绝对优势?解释一下

p264.original: How does comparative advantage lead to gains from trade?
p264.zh: 比较优势如何带来贸易收益?

p266.original: You just overheard your friend say the following: “Poor countries like Malawi have no absolute advantages. They have poor soil, low investments in formal education and hence low-skill workers, no capital, and no natural resources to speak of. Because they have no advantage, they cannot benefit from trade.” How would you respond?

p283.zh: 类似经济体之间的工业内部贸易

p284.original: Absolute and comparative advantages explain a great deal about global trading patterns. For example, they help to explain the patterns that we noted at the start of this chapter, like why you may be eating fresh fruit from Chile or Mexico, or why lower productivity regions like Africa and Latin America are able to sell a substantial proportion of their exports to higher productivity regions like the European Union and North America. Comparative advantage, however, at least at first glance, does not seem especially well-suited to explain other common patterns of international trade.
p284.zh: 绝对和比较优势是全球贸易模式的很大原因。 例如,它们有助于解释我们在本章开头所注意到的模式,比如为什么你们可能吃智利或墨西哥新鲜水果,或者为什么非洲和拉丁美洲等生产力较低的地区能够将其出口品的很大一部分出售给欧洲联盟和北美等生产力较高的地区。 然而,比较优势,至少乍一看,似乎并不特别适合解释国际贸易的其他共同模式。

p285.original: The Prevalence of Intra-Industry Trade between Similar Economies
p285.zh: 类似经济体之间的工业内部贸易的普及程度

p286.original: The theory of comparative advantage suggests that trade should happen between economies with large differences in opportunity costs of production. Roughly half of all U.S. trade involves shipping goods between the fairly similar high-income economies of Japan, Canada, and the United States. Furthermore, the trade has an important geographic component—the biggest trading partners of the United States are Canada and Mexico (see ).
p286.zh: 比较优势理论表明,贸易应当发生在生产机会成本差异较大的经济体之间。大约一半的美国贸易涉及日本、加拿大和美国等相当类似的高收入经济体之间的货运货物。 此外,该贸易具有重要的地域组成部分——美国最大的贸易伙伴是加拿大和墨西哥(见......)。

p306.original: Moreover, the theory of comparative advantage suggests that each economy should specialize to a degree in certain products, and then exchange those products. A high proportion of trade, however, is intra-industry trade—that is, trade of goods within the same industry from one country to another. For example, the United States produces and exports autos and imports autos.  shows some of the largest categories of U.S. exports and imports. In all of these categories, the United States is both a substantial exporter and a substantial importer of goods from the same industry. In 2021, according to the U.S. Census Bureau, the United States exported $131 billion worth of autos, and imported $317 billion worth of autos. About 60% of U.S. trade and 60% of European trade is intra-industry trade.
p306.zh: 此外,比较优势理论表明,每个经济体应在某种程度上专门研究某些产品,然后交换这些产品。 然而,贸易的很大比例是工业内部贸易,即同一工业内的货物从一国到另一国的贸易。 例如,美国生产和出口汽车和进口汽车,显示了美国进出口的一些最大类别。 在所有这些类别中,美国既是大批出口者,也是来自同一行业的大量货物进口者。2021年,据美国报道.人口普查局,美国出口了价值1,310亿美元的汽车,并进口了价值3,170亿美元的汽车. 美国约60%的贸易和欧洲约60%的贸易是产业内贸易.

p307.original: Some Intra-Industry U.S. Exports and Imports in 2021
p307.zh: 美国工业内部的一些企业。2021年进出口

p329.original: Why do similar high-income economies engage in intra-industry trade? What can be the economic benefit of having workers of fairly similar skills making cars, computers, machinery and other products which are then shipped across the oceans to and from the United States, the European Union, and Japan? There are two reasons: (1) The division of labor leads to learning, innovation, and unique skills; and (2) economies of scale.
p329.zh: 为什么类似的高收入经济体从事工业内部贸易? 让工人拥有相当相似的汽车、计算机、机械和其他产品制造技能,然后通过海洋运往美国、欧洲联盟和日本,这有什么经济好处?有两个原因:(1)劳动分工导致学习,创新,和独特的技能;(2)规模经济.

p331.original: Consider the category of machinery, where the U.S. economy has considerable intra-industry trade. Machinery comes in many varieties, so the United States may be exporting machinery for manufacturing with wood, but importing machinery for photographic processing. The underlying reason why a country like the United States, Japan, or Germany produces one kind of machinery rather than another is usually not related to U.S., German, or Japanese firms and workers having generally higher or lower skills. It is just that, in working on very specific and particular products, firms in certain countries develop unique and different skills.
p331.zh: 考虑一下机器这一类,在美国经济中,工业内部贸易相当可观.机械有多种品种,因此美国可能出口机械,用于木材制造,但进口机械用于摄影加工. 美国、日本或德国等国家生产一种机械而不是另一种机械的根本原因通常与美国、德国或拥有一般较高或较低技能的日本公司和工人无关。只是在研究非常具体和特殊产品时,某些国家的公司发展出独特和不同的技能。

p332.original: Specialization in the world economy can be very finely split. In fact, recent years have seen a trend in international trade, which economists call splitting up the value chain. The value chain describes how a good is produced in stages. As indicated in the beginning of the chapter, producing the iPhone involves designing and engineering the phone in the United States, supplying parts from Korea, assembling the parts in China, and advertising and marketing in the United States. Thanks in large part to improvements in communication technology, sharing information, and transportation, it has become easier to split up the value chain. Instead of production in a single large factory, different firms operating in various places and even different countries can divide the value chain. Because firms split up the value chain, international trade often does not involve nations trading whole finished products like automobiles or refrigerators. Instead, it involves shipping more specialized goods like, say, automobile dashboards or the shelving that fits inside refrigerators. Intra-industry trade between similar countries produces economic gains because it allows workers and firms to learn and innovate on particular products—and often to focus on very particular parts of the value chain.
p332.zh: 世界经济专业化可以非常细微地分化. 事实上,近年来,国际贸易出现了一种趋势,经济学家称之为分化价值链。价值链描述了如何分阶段生产商品。 如本章开头所述,生产iPhone涉及在美国设计和制造电话,从韩国供应零件,在中国组装零件,以及在美国进行广告和营销。在很大程度上,由于通信技术、信息共享和运输方面的改进,将价值链分成两部分变得比较容易。不同地方甚至不同国家的不同企业,与其在一家大型工厂生产,不如把价值链分割开来。 由于公司将价值链分割开来,国际贸易往往不涉及诸如汽车或冰箱等整个成品贸易的国家。 相反,它涉及运输更专业的货物,例如汽车仪表板或符合冰箱内部的套装。类似国家之间产业间贸易产生经济收益,因为它使工人和公司能够学习特定产品并进行创新,而且往往侧重于价值链中非常特殊的部分。

p333.original: Visit this website for some interesting information about the assembly of the iPhone.
p333.zh: 访问这个网站,了解有关iPhone组装的一些有趣的信息.

p334.zh: 规模经济、竞争经济、多样性经济

p335.original: A second broad reason that intra-industry trade between similar nations produces economic gains involves economies of scale. The concept of economies of scale, as we introduced in Production, Costs and Industry Structure, means that as the scale of output goes up, average costs of production decline—at least up to a point.  illustrates economies of scale for a plant producing toaster ovens. The horizontal axis of the figure shows the quantity of production by a certain firm or at a certain manufacturing plant. The vertical axis measures the average cost of production. Production plant S produces a small level of output at 30 units and has an average cost of production of $30 per toaster oven. Plant M produces at a medium level of output at 50 units, and has an average cost of production of $20 per toaster oven. Plant L produces 150 units of output with an average cost of production of only $10 per toaster oven. Although plant V can produce 200 units of output, it still has the same unit cost as Plant L.
p335.zh: 类似国家之间工业内部贸易产生经济利益的第二个广泛原因涉及规模经济。 正如我们在《生产、成本和工业结构》中介绍的那样,规模经济的概念意味着,随着产出规模的扩大,平均生产成本下降——至少达到一点。 图中的横向轴线显示的是某家公司或某制造厂的生产数量。纵向轴线衡量平均生产成本.S生产厂以30个单位生产少量产出,每个烤炉平均生产成本为30美元.M厂以50个单位的中等产出水平生产,每个烤炉平均生产成本为20美元.L厂生产150个产出单位,平均每个烤箱生产成本只有10美元. 虽然V厂可以生产200个单位的输出,但它的单位成本仍然与L厂相同.

p336.original: In this example, a small or medium plant, like S or M, will not be able to compete in the market with a large or a very large plant like L or V, because the firm that operates L or V will be able to produce and sell its output at a lower price. In this example, economies of scale operate up to point L, but beyond point L to V, the additional scale of production does not continue to reduce average costs of production.
p336.zh: 在这个例子中,像S或M这样的中小型工厂将无法在市场上与像L或V这样的大型或非常大的工厂竞争,因为经营L或V的公司能够以较低的价格生产和销售其产出. 在这个例子中,规模经济运行到L点,但超过L点到V点,额外的生产规模不会继续降低平均生产成本.

p338.original: The concept of economies of scale becomes especially relevant to international trade when it enables one or two large producers to supply the entire country. For example, a single large automobile factory could probably supply all the cars consumers purchase in a smaller economy like the United Kingdom or Belgium in a given year. However, if a country has only one or two large factories producing cars, and no international trade, then consumers in that country would have relatively little choice between kinds of cars (other than the color of the paint and other nonessential options). Little or no competition will exist between different car manufacturers.
p338.zh: 规模经济的概念在使一两个大生产者能够供应整个国家时,就特别与国际贸易相关。 例如,一个单一的大型汽车工厂可能在某一年里向像联合王国或比利时这样的较小经济体的消费者提供购买的所有汽车。 然而,如果一个国家只有一两个大型的汽车制造厂,而且没有国际贸易,那么该国的消费者在各类汽车(除油漆的颜色和其他非基本选择之外)之间就没有什么选择余地了。不同汽车制造商之间的竞争很少或根本不存在。

p339.original: International trade provides a way to combine the lower average production costs that come from economies of scale and still have competition and variety for consumers. Large automobile factories in different countries can make and sell their products around the world. If General Motors, Ford, and Chrysler were the only players in the U.S. automobile market, the level of competition and consumer choice would be considerably lower than when U.S. carmakers must face competition from Toyota, Honda, Suzuki, Fiat, Mitsubishi, Nissan, Volkswagen, Kia, Hyundai, BMW, Subaru, and others. Greater competition brings with it innovation and responsiveness to what consumers want. America’s car producers make far better cars now than they did several decades ago, and much of the reason is competitive pressure, especially from East Asian and European carmakers.
p339.zh: 国际贸易提供了一种将规模经济产生的较低平均生产成本结合起来的办法,这种成本对于消费者来说仍然具有竞争和多样性。不同国家的大型汽车工厂可以在世界各地制造和销售其产品. 如果通用汽车公司,福特公司,克莱斯勒公司是美国汽车市场中唯一一个参赛者,那么竞争水平和消费者选择水平将大大低于美国汽车制造商必须面对丰田,本田,铃木,菲亚特,三菱,尼山,大众汽车,基亚,现代,宝马,苏巴鲁等的竞争.更大的竞争带来了创新和对消费者所希望的响应。 美国的汽车生产商现在比几十年前的汽车生产量要好得多,大部分原因是竞争压力,特别是东亚和欧洲的汽车生产商。

p341.original: The sources of gains from intra-industry trade between similar economies—namely, the learning that comes from a high degree of specialization and splitting up the value chain and from economies of scale—do not contradict the earlier theory of comparative advantage. Instead, they help to broaden the concept.
p341.zh: 类似经济体之间的产业内部贸易收益的来源,即高度专业化和价值链分化以及规模经济的学习,并不与早先的比较优势理论相矛盾。 相反,它们有助于扩大这一概念。

p342.original: In intra-industry trade, climate or geography do not determine the level of worker productivity. Even the general level of education or skill does not determine it. Instead, how firms engage in specific learning about specialized products, including taking advantage of economies of scale determine the level of worker productivity. In this vision, comparative advantage can be dynamic—that is, it can evolve and change over time as one develops new skills and as manufacturers split the value chain in new ways. This line of thinking also suggests that countries are not destined to have the same comparative advantage forever, but must instead be flexible in response to ongoing changes in comparative advantage.
p342.zh: 在产业内部贸易中,气候或地理并不决定工人的生产力水平. 即使普通教育或技能水平也不决定这一点。 相反,企业如何具体学习专门产品,包括利用规模经济,决定了工人的生产力水平。 在这个愿景中,比较优势可以是动态的,即随着发展新的技能,随着制造商以新的方式分割价值链,它可以随着时间推移而演变和变化。 这一思路还表明,各国注定不会永远拥有同样的比较优势,相反,它们必须灵活地应对不断发生的比较优势变化。

p344.original: A large share of global trade happens between high-income economies that are quite similar in having well-educated workers and advanced technology. These countries practice intra-industry trade, in which they import and export the same products at the same time, like cars, machinery, and computers. In the case of intra-industry trade between economies with similar income levels, the gains from trade come from specialized learning in very particular tasks and from economies of scale. Splitting up the value chain means that several stages of producing a good take place in different countries around the world.
p344.zh: 全球贸易的很大一部分发生在高收入经济体之间,这些经济体拥有受过良好教育的工人和先进技术。这些国家实行工业内部贸易,它们同时进出口相同的产品,如汽车、机械和计算机。 就收入水平类似的经济体之间的产业内部贸易而言,贸易收益来自对非常特殊任务的专门学习和规模经济。分解价值链意味着生产商品的几个阶段发生在世界各国。

p346.original: How can there be any economic gains for a country from both importing and exporting the same good, like cars?
p346.zh: 一个国家怎么可能从同样货物,例如汽车的进口和出口中获得任何经济利益?

p347.original: There are a number of possible advantages of intra-industry trade. Both nations can take advantage of extreme specialization and learning in certain kinds of cars with certain traits, like gas-efficient cars, luxury cars, sport-utility vehicles, higher- and lower-quality cars, and so on. Moreover, nations can take advantage of economies of scale, so that large companies will compete against each other across international borders, providing the benefits of competition and variety to customers. This same argument applies to trade between U.S. states, where people often buy products made by people of other states, even though a similar product is made within the boundaries of their own state. All states—and all countries—can benefit from this kind of competition and trade.
p347.zh: 工业内部贸易可能有一些好处。两国可以利用某种具有一定特点的汽车的极端专业化和学习,如节气汽车,豪华汽车,运动实用汽车,高品质和低品质汽车等. 此外,各国可以利用规模经济,使大公司跨越国际边界相互竞争,为客户提供竞争和多样性的好处。 这个论点同样适用于美国各州之间的贸易,美国人经常购买其他国家人民制造的产品,尽管类似的产品是在他们自己的国家边界内制造的.所有国家——以及所有国家——都可以从这种竞争和贸易中受益。

p348.original: shows how the average costs of production for semiconductors (the “chips” in computer memories) change as the quantity of semiconductors built at that factory increases.

Start by plotting the points on a sketch diagram and then drawing a line through them. The following figure illustrates the average costs of production of semiconductors.



  The curve illustrates economies of scale by showing that as the scale increases—that is, as production at this particular factory goes up—the average cost of production declines. p365.original: At any quantity demanded above 40,000, this economy can take full advantage of economies of scale; that is, it can produce at the lowest cost per unit. Indeed, if the quantity demanded was quite high, like 500,000, then there could be a number of different factories all taking full advantage of economies of scale and competing with each other. If the quantity demanded falls below 40,000, then the economy by itself, without foreign trade, cannot take full advantage of economies of scale.
p365.zh: 在40,000以上的需求量中,这种经济可以充分利用规模经济;也就是说,它可以以最低的单位成本生产。 事实上,如果所要求的数量相当高,如50万,那么,就可能有一些不同的工厂都充分利用规模经济,相互竞争。 如果所需数量低于4万,那么,没有外贸,经济本身就不能充分利用规模经济。

p366.original: The simplest answer to this question is that the small country could have a large enough factory to take full advantage of economies of scale, but then export most of the output. For semiconductors, countries like Taiwan and Korea have recently fit this description. Moreover, this country could also import semiconductors from other countries which also have large factories, thus getting the benefits of competition and variety. A slightly more complex answer is that the country can get these benefits of economies of scale without producing semiconductors, but simply by buying semiconductors made at low cost around the world. An economy, especially a smaller country, may well end up specializing and producing a few items on a large scale, but then trading those items for other items produced on a large scale, and thus gaining the benefits of economies of scale by trade, as well as by direct production.
p366.zh: 这个问题最简单的答案是,小国可以拥有一个足够大的工厂,充分利用规模经济,但随后出口大部分产出. 对于半导体来说,台湾和韩国等国家最近都符合这一描述. 此外,该国还可以从拥有大型工厂的其他国家进口半导体,从而获得竞争和品种的好处。 一个稍复杂一点的答案是,该国可以不生产半导体而从规模经济中获得这些好处,但只需购买世界各地低成本制造的半导体即可。 一个经济体,特别是小国,最终很可能会大规模地专门生产和生产几件物品,但随后将这些物品换成大规模生产的其他物品,从而通过贸易以及直接生产获得规模经济的好处。

p382.original: The Benefits of Reducing Barriers to International Trade
p382.zh: 减少国际贸易障碍的益处

p383.original: Tariffs are taxes that governments place on imported goods for a variety of reasons. Some of these reasons include protecting sensitive industries, for humanitarian reasons, and protecting against dumping. Traditionally, tariffs were used simply as a political tool to protect certain vested economic, social, and cultural interests. The World Trade Organization (WTO) is committed to lowering barriers to trade. The world’s nations meet through the WTO to negotiate how they can reduce barriers to trade, such as tariffs. WTO negotiations happen in “rounds,” where all countries negotiate one agreement to encourage trade, take a year or two off, and then start negotiating a new agreement. The current round of negotiations is called the Doha Round because it was officially launched in Doha, the capital city of Qatar, in November 2001. In 2010, the WTO noted that the Doha Round’s emphasis on market access and reforms of agricultural subsidies could add $121–$202 billion to the world economy.
p383.zh: 关税是指政府出于各种原因对进口货物征收的税费.其中一些原因包括出于人道主义原因保护敏感产业,以及防止倾销。传统上,关税只是作为保护某些既得经济、社会和文化利益的政治工具。世界贸易组织(世贸组织)致力于降低贸易壁垒。世界各国通过世贸组织开会,商讨如何减少关税等贸易壁垒。世贸组织的谈判是在“回合”中进行的,在“回合”中,所有国家都谈判一项协定以鼓励贸易,但需要一年或两年的时间,然后开始谈判一项新的协定。 本轮谈判被称为多哈回合,因为多哈回合于2001年11月在卡塔尔首都多哈正式启动。2010年,世贸组织指出,多哈回合对市场准入和农业补贴改革的重视可给世界经济增加1 21亿至2 200亿美元。

p384.original:
In the context of a global economy that currently produces more than $80 trillion of goods and services each year, this amount is not large: it is an increase of less than 1%. But before dismissing the gains from trade too quickly, it is worth remembering two points.
  
First, a gain of a few hundred billion dollars is enough money to deserve attention! Moreover, remember that this increase is not a one-time event; it would persist each year into the future.
Second, the estimate of gains may be on the low side because some of the gains from trade are not measured especially well in economic statistics. For example, it is difficult to measure the potential advantages to consumers of having a variety of products available and a greater degree of competition among producers. Perhaps the most important unmeasured factor is that trade between countries, especially when firms are splitting up the value chain of production, often involves a transfer of knowledge that can involve skills in production, technology, management, finance, and law.
p384.zh: 在目前每年生产80万亿美元以上的货物和服务的全球经济中,这一数额并不大:增长不到1%。 但是,在过早地放弃贸易收益之前,值得记住两点。 首先,赚到几千亿美元,就足以引起人们的注意! 此外,要记住,这种增加不是一次性事件;它每年将持续到未来。 第二,估计收益可能处于低水平,因为从贸易中获得的某些收益在经济统计中衡量得特别差。 例如,难以衡量消费者获得各种产品和生产者之间更大程度竞争的潜在好处。最重要的未计量因素是,国家之间的贸易,特别是在公司正在分割生产价值链的情况下,往往涉及知识的转让,涉及生产、技术、管理、金融和法律方面的技能。

p385.original: Low-income countries benefit more from trade than high-income countries do. In some ways, the giant U.S. economy has less need for international trade, because it can already take advantage of internal trade within its economy. However, many smaller national economies around the world, in regions like Latin America, Africa, the Middle East, and Asia, have much more limited possibilities for trade inside their countries or their immediate regions. Without international trade, they may have little ability to benefit from comparative advantage, slicing up the value chain, or economies of scale. Moreover, smaller economies often have fewer competitive firms making goods within their economy, and thus firms have less pressure from other firms to provide the goods and prices that consumers want.
p385.zh: 低收入国家比高收入国家从贸易中受益更多。在某些方面,美国巨型经济对国际贸易的需求较少,因为它已经能够利用其经济内部贸易的优势. 然而,在拉丁美洲、非洲、中东和亚洲等区域,世界上许多较小的国家经济在其国家或直接区域内的贸易机会要有限得多。 没有国际贸易,它们可能就没有什么能力从比较优势、分解价值链或规模经济中获益。 此外,较小的经济体的竞争性企业往往较少,而在其经济中制造商品,因此,其他企业对提供消费者想要的商品和价格的压力较小。

p386.original: The economic gains from expanding international trade are measured in hundreds of billions of dollars, and the gains from international trade as a whole probably reach well into the trillions of dollars. The potential for gains from trade may be especially high among the smaller and lower-income countries of the world.
p386.zh: 扩大国际贸易的经济收益以数千亿美元衡量,国际贸易整体收益可能远达万亿美元。贸易收益在世界较小和低收入国家中可能特别大。

p388.zh: 从人际贸易到国际贸易

p389.original: Most people find it easy to believe that they, personally, would not be better off if they tried to grow and process all of their own food, to make all of their own clothes, to build their own cars and houses from scratch, and so on. Instead, we all benefit from living in economies where people and firms can specialize and trade with each other.
p389.zh: 多数人觉得很容易相信,如果自己试图种植和加工所有自己的食物,制造所有自己的衣服,从零开始建造自己的汽车和房屋等等,他们个人就不会更好了. 相反,我们都从生活在人们和公司可以专门从事彼此贸易的经济中受益。

p390.original: The benefits of trade do not stop at national boundaries, either. Earlier we explained that the division of labor could increase output for three reasons: (1) workers with different characteristics can specialize in the types of production where they have a comparative advantage; (2) firms and workers who specialize in a certain product become more productive with learning and practice; and (3) economies of scale. These three reasons apply from the individual and community level right up to the international level. If it makes sense to you that interpersonal, intercommunity, and interstate trade offer economic gains, it should make sense that international trade offers gains, too.
p390.zh: 贸易的好处也不局限于国界。 我们早些时候解释过,分工可以增加产出,原因有三:(1)具有不同特点的工人可以专门从事他们具有比较优势的生产类型;(2)专门从事某一产品的公司和工人随着学习和实践而提高生产率;(3)规模经济. 从个人和社区一级一直到国际一级,这三项理由都适用。 如果对你们来说,人际、社区间和国家间贸易能带来经济收益是有意义的,那么国际贸易也能带来利益。

p391.original: International trade currently involves about $20 trillion worth of goods and services moving around the globe. Any economic force of that size, even if it confers overall benefits, is certain to cause disruption and controversy. This chapter has only made the case that trade brings economic benefits. Other chapters discuss, in detail, the public policy arguments over whether to restrict international trade.
p391.zh: 国际贸易目前涉及价值20万亿美元的货物和服务,它们在全球各地流动。 这种规模的任何经济力量,即使带来整体利益,也必然造成混乱和争议。 这一章只是说明贸易带来经济利益。 其他章节详细讨论了公共政策对是否限制国际贸易的论点。

p393.original: Apple Corporation uses a global platform to produce the iPhone. Now that you understand the concept of comparative advantage, you can see why the engineering and design of the iPhone is done in the United States. The United States has built up a comparative advantage over the years in designing and marketing products, and sacrifices fewer resources to design high-tech devices relative to other countries. China has a comparative advantage in assembling the phone due to its large skilled labor force. Korea has a comparative advantage in producing components. Korea focuses its production by increasing its scale, learning better ways to produce screens and computer chips, and uses innovation to lower average costs of production. Apple, in turn, benefits because it can purchase these quality products at lower prices. Put the global assembly line together and you have the device with which we are all so familiar.
p393.zh: Apple Corporation使用全球平台生产iPhone. 既然你理解了比较优势的概念,你就能理解为什么iPhone的工程和设计在美国完成.多年来,美国在设计和销售产品方面积累了比较优势,并牺牲了比其他国家更少的资源来设计高技术装置。 由于中国拥有庞大的熟练劳动力,因此在电话组装方面具有比较优势。韩国在生产部件方面有比较优势.韩国通过扩大规模,学习更好的生产屏幕和计算机芯片的方法,并运用创新来降低平均生产成本,从而集中生产.苹果反过来也带来好处,因为它可以低价购买这些优质产品. 把全球组装线合在一起 你拥有我们都熟悉的装置

p395.original: Tariffs are placed on imported goods as a way of protecting sensitive industries, for humanitarian reasons, and for protection against dumping. Traditionally, tariffs were used as a political tool to protect certain vested economic, social, and cultural interests. The WTO has been, and continues to be, a way for nations to meet and negotiate in order to reduce barriers to trade. The gains of international trade are very large, especially for smaller countries, but are beneficial to all.
p395.zh: 对进口货物实行关税,作为出于人道主义原因保护敏感产业和防止倾销的一种方式。传统上,关税被用作保护某些既得经济、社会和文化利益的政治工具。世贸组织一直是,而且将继续是各国为减少贸易壁垒而开会和谈判的一种方式。国际贸易的收益非常巨大,对小国尤其如此,但惠及所有国家。

p397.original: If the removal of trade barriers is so beneficial to international economic growth, why would a nation continue to restrict trade on some imported or exported products?
p397.zh: 如果消除贸易壁垒对国际经济增长如此有利,一个国家为什么继续限制某些进出口产品的贸易?

p398.original: A nation might restrict trade on imported products to protect an industry that is important for national security.  For example, nation X and nation Y may be geopolitical rivals, each with ambitions of increased political and economic strength.  Even if nation Y has comparative advantage in the production of missile defense systems, it is unlikely that nation Y would seek to export those goods to nation X.  It is also the case that, for some nations, the production of a particular good is a key component of national identity.  In Japan, the production of rice is culturally very important.  It may be difficult for Japan to import rice from a nation like Vietnam, even if Vietnam has a comparative advantage in rice production.
p398.zh: 一个国家可能限制进口产品的贸易,以保护对国家安全至关重要的行业。 例如,X国和Y国可能是地缘政治的对手,它们各自都有增加政治和经济实力的野心。 即使Y国在导弹防御系统的生产方面拥有比较优势,Y国也不太可能寻求将这些货物出口到X国. 对一些国家来说,生产某种物品是民族特性的关键组成部分。 在日本,水稻的生产在文化上非常重要. 日本可能难以从越南这样的国家进口水稻,即使越南在水稻生产方面拥有比较优势.

p406.original: If trade increases world GDP by 1% per year, what is the global impact of this increase over 10 years? How does this increase compare to the annual GDP of a country like Sri Lanka? c1.zh: (a) 沙特阿拉伯可生产100桶最高和零玉米(A点)的石油,或25桶玉米和零石油(B点)。 如果它想消耗两种商品,例如C点,它也可以生产其他的石油和玉米组合. 在此,它选择生产/制造60桶石油,留下40个工时,用其中的数据来生产10只小毛耳玉米。(b) 如果美国只生产石油,它最多可以生产50桶和零玉米(A点),或者在另一极端,它最多可以生产100匹小毛耳的玉米,没有石油(B点)。石油和玉米的其他组合也是可能的,如点C'. 鉴于目前的资源和技术水平,边界上的所有点都不可能产生。

c2.original: Trade allows a country to go beyond its domestic production-possibility frontier
c2.zh: 贸易使一个国家能够超越其国内生产可能性的边界

c3.original: (a) With 40 workers, the United States can produce either 10,000 shoes and zero refrigerators or 40,000 refrigerators and zero shoes. (b) With 40 workers, Mexico can produce a maximum of 8,000 shoes and zero refrigerators, or 10,000 refrigerators and zero shoes. All other points on the production possibility line are possible combinations of the two goods that can be produced given current resources. Point A on both graphs is where the countries start producing and consuming before trade. Point B is where they end up after trade.
c3.zh: (a) 有40名工人,美国可以生产1万双鞋和零冰箱,或4万只冰箱和零鞋。 有40名工人,墨西哥最多可生产8000双鞋和零冰箱,或10,000只冰箱和零鞋子. 关于生产可能性线的所有其他要点都是根据现有资源可以生产的两种商品的可能组合。 这两个图上的A点是国家在贸易前开始生产和消费的地方。B点是交易结束后的结局

c7.original: Production Plant S, has an average cost of production of $30 per toaster oven. Production plant M has an average cost of production of $20 per toaster oven. Production plant L has an average cost of production of only $10 per toaster oven. Production plant V still has an average cost of production of $10 per toaster oven. Thus, production plant M can produce toaster ovens more cheaply than plant S because of economies of scale, and plants L or V can produce more cheaply than S or M because of economies of scale. However, the economies of scale end at an output level of 150. Plant V, despite being larger, cannot produce more cheaply on average than plant L.
c7.zh: 生产厂S,平均生产成本为每炉30美元.M生产厂每烤炉平均生产成本为20美元。L生产厂平均每个烤箱生产成本只有10美元。V生产厂的平均生产成本仍为每烤炉10美元。 因此,由于规模经济,M生产厂可以比S生产烤炉更便宜,L或V生产厂可以比S或M生产更便宜,因为规模经济. 然而,规模经济最终产出为150。V厂虽然规模较大,但平均产量不能比L厂更便宜.
